prize_parts.citation: for the magic-wavelength optical lattice clock and its realisation at a fractional uncertainty of 10^-18
for the discovery of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos with the IceCube observatory

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange I keep my two-part configuration, but I have changed how I defend it. B029 is now the part I would defend to anyone: the magic-wavelength lattice clock is a clear original idea (Katori) carried to a quantitative frontier (Ye), reproduced and compared at the 10^-18 level by JILA, RIKEN, PTB, NIST and SYRTE, and four of eight members already prefer it with the identical pair. Following Pearce and Kroll I would word the citation around the lattice scheme and its realisation at 10^-18, so that the comb (2005) and single-ion (2012) prizes are not implicitly re-awarded, and I would keep the redefinition of the second and geodesy out of the citation: they are prospects, not results. The second part, B037, rests on one thing only: the discovery of a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos at energies up to the PeV scale, established by IceCube and confirmed by several independent analyses and channels. That is a clue from nature of exactly the kind I want, an entirely new window, and it is a discovery that does not depend on identifying the sources. I have therefore narrowed the citation from 'creation of neutrino astronomy' to the flux itself, which removes the weak points (TXS 0506+056 at about 3 sigma, a recent Galactic-plane result). Three names, two distinct achievements, no more than the rule allows.
statement.case_against: B037 remains the weakest link and I say so plainly: no other member includes it, only Pearce ranks it second, and a single laureate for a collaboration of hundreds, with an AMANDA precursor and earlier deep-water and deep-ice efforts, is exposed to the charge of understating others. I also cannot show that the two parts share any scientific kinship beyond both being new ways of probing nature; the pairing is partly a consequence of the three-name limit, and the chair is right to ask about it. If colleagues judge that Halzen alone cannot be defended, the honest outcome is B029 as the whole prize, or B029 with B031 as the stronger-supported second part, not a different single name for IceCube that the shortlist does not offer. On B029, the novelty question against 2005 and 2012 and the open proposal-history credit (Lemonde, Peik, Hollberg) are real, and I would want the outside assessment I would normally commission as Secretary before the committee fixes the two names.

responses.point: The chair asked whether Halzen as sole credit for B037 can be defended, and noted that the TXS association is about 3 sigma, the Galactic-plane result is recent and the origin of most of the flux is unknown.
responses.response: I accept the last three points and have cut them out of my citation: the prize part would be for the diffuse flux, which is not in doubt, and not for source astronomy. On Halzen, I can defend him as the conceiver and persistent leader of the cubic-kilometre ice detector from AMANDA to IceCube, but I cannot claim the record settles that he is the only person; you have flagged your own adjacency to B037, so I ask you to say whether you would step back if it became decisive. On B029 I agree with your wording point and have adopted it. I also note you and I now agree that Higgs detector leadership is a weaker route than clean attribution, so I have moved B012 out of my alternatives.

responses.point: Eriksson separates the discovery of correlated and superconducting phases from the unresolved mechanism, and says we recognised superconductivity before its mechanism was understood.
responses.response: That is a fair rebuttal and it weakens my timing objection: I accept that the phenomenon is reproduced and that an open pairing mechanism is not by itself disqualifying. What still stops me from moving B031 into my preferred set is the credit, because the lead experimental authors and Dean's group are outside the trio and the theory credit is contested between a two-name and a three-name version, as you and Olsson concede. Your own point that device-to-device variability from twist-angle disorder affects which phases appear is the thing I would want an outside expert to settle. I therefore moved B031 to my first alternative in place of B012; if the condensed-matter members can agree on the credited set, it becomes my second part or my replacement for B037.

responses.point: Mehlig regards the clock as a close alternative but a refinement of the ruler the 2005 and 2012 prizes created, while moire graphene opens a new regime of matter.
responses.response: I take the distinction between a refinement and a new regime seriously, but I would not call the lattice clock a mere refinement: the many-atom magic-wavelength scheme is a different route past the single-ion quantum-projection limit, and it is the clock comparisons that now probe relativistic redshift over millimetres. I also note that you yourself called its attribution cleaner than that of B031, and said B029 is the cleaner fallback if the B031 credit set is judged unsound. Since my two parts do not compete with your first choice for the same slot, I ask you to say whether you could accept B031 as a second part beside B029, which would use the three names only if the theory credit is two, not three.

responses.point: Kroll wants the B029 citation written around the measurement achievement (control of systematics to 1e-18), not only the idea, and asks whether to wait for the redefinition of the second.
responses.response: I agree with the citation being about the achievement, and I have written mine as 'the magic-wavelength optical lattice clock and its realisation at 10^-18'. I would not wait for the redefinition: the cross-laboratory comparisons already show the result, and I would rather the committee not make its decision depend on a metrology-body vote. Where I still differ is on the geodesy and dark-matter reach, which I would keep out of the citation. You have also noted your year in Hall's laboratory; since Hall is not a credited name I do not see it as disqualifying, but please say whether the outside assessment of Lemonde, Peik and Hollberg changes your view of the two names.

responses.point: Olsson ranks B029 last, argues that the 2005 and 2012 prizes already covered the territory and that the benefit to humanity is modest, and she wants priority and credit checked before anything is fixed.
responses.response: I share your insistence on checking priority, which is why I would commission outside assessments for B029 and for the IceCube credit before the vote. But I would not use benefit to humanity as the test: the Prize is for discovery, and I would weigh the clocks on demonstrated reproduced performance, which I think you accept, since you name B029 as an alternative for exactly its experimental maturity. On B001, I agree with you that Wrachtrup and Jelezko is the cleaner credit, but I find the discovery boundary against Hanson and Awschalom still unclear and I do not rank it above my parts.

responses.point: Lindroth, as an atomic physicist, regards the lattice scheme as a different physical route from Wineland's single-ion methods and distinct from the 2005 comb prize.
responses.response: I find that argument convincing and it is the one I would use publicly: a magic wavelength is an atomic-structure concept, and the many-atom statistics are what the ion clocks lack. I would press you on the one question the chair left to you, whether Katori and Ye are an adequate pair given Lemonde, Peik and Hollberg on the proposal side and Ludlow, Bloom and Lemke on the achievement side. If you and Kroll confirm that the proposal history does not change the two names, I will treat B029 as settled, and then the only open issue in my configuration is whether the committee wants a second part at all.

uncertainties: Whether Francis Halzen alone is an acceptable credit for the IceCube flux discovery, or whether an outside assessment would show that other names (for example from AMANDA) belong with him.
Whether the committee wants a second part at all; if not, I would support B029 alone, and if B031's credited set can be settled I would prefer it over B037.
Whether the proposal history (Lemonde, Peik, Hollberg) and the team contributions to the 10^-18 milestone leave Katori and Ye as the right two names.
How much weight the 2005 and 2012 prizes should carry against B029.
Whether pairing precision metrology with astroparticle physics reads as an arbitrary pairing, driven by the three-name limit.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict with any shortlisted candidate. My PhD supervisor David Gross and co-author Thomas Van Riet work in string theory and cosmology, unconnected to B029, B037, B031 or B016. As Secretary I would normally commission outside expert reports, and I note that I have not seen any here, so my judgement of the credit rests on the committee's own statements.
